extraction.name: CoNLL-2003 Shared Task: Language-Independent Named Entity Recognition
extraction.description: A named entity recognition dataset consisting of English and German data split into training, development, and test sets, along with unannotated text. The annotation identifies four types of named entities: persons (PER), locations (LOC), organizations (ORG), and miscellaneous names (MISC).
extraction.creator: Erik F. Tjong Kim Sang and Fien De Meulder
extraction.citeAs: Erik F. Tjong Kim Sang and Fien De Meulder. 2003. Introduction to the CoNLL-2003 Shared Task: Language-Independent Named Entity Recognition. In Proceedings of CoNLL-2003.
extraction.rai:dataCollection: The English data was extracted from the Reuters Corpus, which consists of Reuters news stories between August 1996 and August 1997. The German data was taken from the ECI Multilingual Text Corpus, specifically extracted from the German newspaper Frankfurter Rundschau.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Reuters Corpus (news stories) and ECI Multilingual Text Corpus (Frankfurter Rundschau newspaper articles).
extraction.rai:dataCollectionTimeframe: English data: August 1996 to August 1997 (training and development from late August 1996, test from December 1996, raw unannotated from September 1996). German data: late August 1992 (raw unannotated from September to December 1992).
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Linguistic preprocessing was performed prior to system access: tokenization using two language-specific tokenizers; English data was part-of-speech tagged and chunked using the memory-based MBT tagger; German data was lemmatized, part-of-speech tagged, and chunked using the decision tree tagger Treetagger. Data was formatted with one word per line in the IOB format containing word, POS tag, chunk tag, and named entity tag.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Named entity tagging was performed by hand at the University of Antwerp following mostly MUC conventions. Four entity categories were labeled: persons (PER), organizations (ORG), locations (LOC), and miscellaneous (MISC). Entities were assumed to be non-recursive and non-overlapping, with only the top-level entity annotated when embedded.
extraction.rai:machineAnnotationTools: MBT tagger (for English POS tagging and chunking), Treetagger (for German lemmatizing, POS tagging, and chunking)
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Training, parameter tuning/validation (development set), and testing/evaluation of machine learning systems for language-independent named entity recognition.
